\\n We propose a new 2-terminal refresh-free memory suitable for 1T-DRAM applications. This memory cell is composed of a multilayer nanowire including silicon (Si), silicon-germanium (SiGe) storage regions and a silicon buffer layer and the nanowire is surrounded by a polysilicon layer. A 2-terminal structure with a 4F\\n 2\\n footprint enables high-density implementation. The valence-band offset at the Si/SiGe heterojunction suppresses hole diffusion in the SiGe storage region, thereby improving hole retention. The polysilicon layer reduces electron inflow, thereby inducing holes to accumulate locally in the SiGe storage region rather than the Si storage region, which reduces impact ionization and retains the state \\\"1\\\". The polysilicon layer enables to form a holding region that can retain data at low power consumption even when using only two electrodes, providing a low standby current of 4.5 pA when retaining state “1” and a wide holding margin with a gradual current slope of 220 mV/dec. This device achieves a memory operation speed within 10 ns. In particular, the buffer layer suppresses excessive hole generation, thereby improving the speed of write \\\"0\\\" operation…
